full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J. This appeal, by leave, is by the defendant No. 2 against the judgment and order dated July 8, 1997 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1788 of 1992 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated April 21, 1992 of the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Jessore in Title Appeal No. 63 of 1986 dismissing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated February 22; 1986 of the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Jihikargacha, Jessore in Title Suit No. 273 of 1984 decreeing the same. The plaintiffs sought for declaration of title in respect of 1.58½ acres of land out of 3.44 acres of land described in the schedule attached to the plaint. Plaintiffs filed the suit stating, inter alia, that land measuring 3.44 acres recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 599 belonged to Pachu Rishi. On his death his son Taru Rishi inherited the testate of Pachu Rishi. He sold 1.581/2 acres of land to the plaintiffs on December 9, 1982. It is the case of the plaintiffs that since their purchase they are in possession of the land by erecting but and planting trees. Defendant No. 1's brother, who is a Tahsilder, in collusion with the employee of the Settlement Department illegally got recorded in defendant No. 1 name 1.67 acres of land including the land in suit and on the basis thereof defendants on December 8, 1983 tried to disturb plaintiffs possession in the land in suit. 

 2. Defendant No. 2, appellant herein, contested the suit stating, inter alia, that the land recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 599 in the name of Pachu Rishi was sold in auction for arrears of rent. After auction sale Pachu Rishi took settlement of 1.77 acres of land of plot Nos. 1863 and 1864 by executing kabuliat dated 16th Falgoon, 1352 B.S. corresponding to February 28, 1946, which was registered on March 5, 1946, in favour of auction purchaser landlord. The auction purchaser landlord settled 1.67 acres of land to the defendant No. 1 in 1359 B.S. and the land so settled to the defendant No. 1 has been recorded as being the land of bata dag No. 3502/3530 in S.A. Khatian No. 714. The defendant No. 1 sold .83 acre of land on May 5, 1968 to the defendant No. 2 (Appellant) and sold the rest to Badal Gazi and Shamsher Gazi, on March 27, 1970 and they sold their purchased land to the defendant No. 2 and thus defendant No. 2 has acquired right, title and possession in 1.67 acres of land including the land in suit. It was also the case of the contesting defendant that Taru Rishi had no right, title and possession in the land and that the kabala by which plaintiffs claimed to have purchased the land from Taru Rishi is a fraudulent one and on the basis of said purchase plaintiffs have not acquired any right, title and possession. 

 3. The Court of 1st instance on consideration of evidence, both oral and documentary, upon arriving at the findings that the suit is not barred by limitation; that Pachu Rishi and after his death his son Taru Rishi had right, title and interest in the land in suit; that the defendant failed to establish by any reliable evidence that land of C.S. Khatian No. 599 i.e. land owned by Pachu Rishi was sold in auction for arrears of rent and that auction purchaser landlord took possession of the said land and as such as Pachu Rishi's right, title and interest in the land in suit did not extinguish; his son Taru Rishi acquired right, title and interest of Pachu Rishi and thereupon having had the right, title and interest sold the land in suit to the plaintiffs and they upon purchase from Taru Rishi have acquired right, title and interest in the land in suit and they have established their case by evidence, both oral and documentary, decreed the suit. 

 5. One of the plaintiffs (plaintiff No. 2) moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division on the findings that on examination of the evidence, both oral and documentary, of the parties it is seen plaintiffs succeeded in proving that Pachu Rishi was the original owner of the land in suit and after death of Pachu Rishi his son Taru Rishi inherited the land as title of Pachu Rishi is admitted by the parties; that in proof of the case of the defendant that Pachu Rishi having had defaulted in the payment of rents landlord put his land of C.S. Khatian No. 599 into auction and purchased the same no paper has been brought on record and that case of the defendant that land of Pachu Rishi was sold in auction and that after purchase by the landlord he settled 1.67 acres of land including the land in suit to the defendant No. 1; vendor of the defendant No. 2, having had not been established, defendant No. 2's claim of title does not stand. The High Court Division also considered the case of the defendant that after auction purchase by the landlord they upon executing Kabuliyat in favour of the landlord took settlement of 1.67 acres of land inclusive of land in suit and has observed "Moreover the claim of the defendant is  further based on a kabuliyat purported to have been executed by them in favour of the landlord. This document being an admittedly unilateral document not followed by any contemporaneous document executed by the landlord it is difficult to accept the evidence as to acquisition of title by them in the suit property solely on the basis of the said kabuliyat. Moreover from the evidence on record it is found that the plaintiffs succeeded to prove their case by producing evidence, oral and documentary". The High Court Division reversed the judgment and decree of the appellate Court upon observing "It is true that the defendants are not required to prove their case and in case of defect the plaintiff cannot take advantage of the same but in the facts and circumstances revealed in the instant suit the defendants claim being not at all supported by any legal evidence and more so the plaintiffs being successful to prove their case, I am of the opinion that the learned Subordinate Judge while disposing of the appeal did not correctly appreciate the facts and circumstances and evidence on record. It further appears that considering the evidence in details the trial court on the basis of the materials passed the judgment with sound reasoning and the court of appeal without reversing the finding of facts with refer mice to any evidence passed the impugned judgment disregarding the law and facts and as such I hold that the impugned judgment passed by the lower appellate Court suffers froth error in the decision occasioning failure of justice". 

 7. The first contention of the learned Counsel for the appellant that appellate Court on consideration of the documents having had held defendant has title and possession of the land in suit, the High Court Division was in error in setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court without setting aside the said finding of the appellate Court is not correct. It seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division did not accept the defendant's claim of acquiring title in the background of non-establishing by producing documentary as well as oral evidence the case of auction sale of recorded tenant's right, title and interest for arrears of rent and of purchasing the land of C.S. Khatian No. 599 by the landlord. The High Court Division discarded the case of the appellant since his vendor who said to have taken settlement from the auction purchaser landlord after C.S. recorded tenant's land haying said to have been sold for arrears of rent, by executing a kabuliyat as because no evidence either documentary or oral was brought on record from the defendant's side as to the fact that the kabuliyat upon executing of which appellant's vendor said to have taken settlement from the so called auction purchaser landlord was acted upon. The admitted and undisputed fact is that Pachu Rishi, the admitted C.S. recorded tenant was the owner of the land in suit as well as some other lands and unless right, title and interest of the C.S. recorded tenant had extinguished, in any manner or in the manner as claimed by the appellant, though there is total absence of material as regards that, there was no occasion for the landlord to settle the land of the recorded tenant to anybody else including the vendor of the appellant and consequently right, title and interest as remained with the admitted owner, the plaintiffs by their purchase from the undisputed sole heir of recorded tenant have acquired good title in the land in suit. The appellant did not at all establish the material fact of losing title by recorded tenant and his sole heir and in the background thereof the trial Court as well as the High Court Division arrived at the finding that Pachu Rishi's right and title was not affected at any time in any, manner and that on the death of Pachu Rishi his son Taru Rishi inherited the land in suit as well as the other land of his father. Because of the afore state of the matter the papers relied on by the appellant in support of his claim in the land in suit are of no worth and on the basis of those papers it cannot be said that appellants vendor and the appellant have acquired right and title in the land which once belonged to Pachu Rishi and thereafter his son Taru Rishi from whom the plaintiffs made the purchase of the land in suit." 

 9. This witness in his cross-examination has stated ‘কবিলিয়ত ভুক্ত ১৮৬০ দাগের উপর পাচু ঋষির বাড়ী ছিল। ------ নালিশী জমিতে কোন গাছপালা ঘর বাড়ী নাই। ঐ সকল গাছগাছালী ১৮৬৪ দাগের উপর পাচু ঋষির বাড়ী ছিল। ------ নালিশী জমিতে কোন গাছপালা ঘর বাড়ী নাই। ঐ সকল গাছগাছালী ১৮৬৪ দাগে আছে। ১৮৬৪ দাগে বাদীদের বাড়ী।------ From the reading of evidence of P.W.4 it is evidenced that said witness in cross has stated নালীশী জমি ধানী জমি। আউষ এবং আমন ধান হয়। এই জমির দক্ষিনে পুকুর আছে। সেই পুকুর ছামাদ সাহেব কেটেছিল এবং দখল করে’ On analysis of the evidence as quoted above it is seen that it can in no way he said that plaintiffs are out of possession of the land in suit. Moreover plaintiffs have claimed 1½ decimals of land out of the land of plot No. 1864 and they are in possession thereof as seen from the evidence on record and that being so the contention of the learned Counsel for the appellant that High Court Division was in error in setting aside the finding of fact arrived at by the appellate Court on the basis of the evidence of P.W. 1 which was corroborated by P.W. 4 that plaintiffs are out of possession of .35 acre of land is not correct. P.W. 4 has stated that land possessed by Samad is to the west of land in suit. It may be mentioned total quantity of land in C.S. Khatian No. 599 corresponding S.A. Khatian No. 713 is 3.44 acres and out of that plaintiff’s are claiming 1.58½ acres. The trial Court on detailed discussions of the evidence of the parties found possession of the land in suit in favour of the plaintiffs. The appellate Court set aside the said finding of the trial Court upon the view that fact of possession of Taru Rishi was not proved by the plaintiffs by producing documentary evidence and that Taru Rishi was not examined by the plaintiffs. The appellate Court as seen from the reading of the judgment of the said Court rejected the oral evidence relating to possession of the land in suit by the plaintiffs upon the consideration which can hardly be considered legally well founded one.
